newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Mar 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Mar 18.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
Loadshedding has forced over 150 mills and factories to suspend their operations in southern industrial belt of Khulna.
Port users on Monday threatened to the Chittagong Port Authority that they would go for an indefinite strike unless private equipment was allowed for unloading cargo.
Iranian Foreign Minister Dr Ali Akbar Velayati arrives in Dhaka on Wednesday on a two-day official visit to Bangladesh.

At least ten people, including five policemen, were injured in southeastern Magura district when police tried to disperse an angry mob who attacked residence of a local electricity official in protest of frequent power cut.
Bangladesh's much-talked 25-year friendship treaty with India expires on Tuesday.
Opposition Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) Secretary General Abdul Mannan Bhuiyan on Monday said that the ruling party had began a "war against an imaginary enemy".
Business community have expressed serious concern at the acute power shortage in the country, saying that they are faced with severe losses due to disruptions in production.
The government and the World Bank on Monday discussed plans for a complete overhauling of the country's banking sector.
